title: Pullman's carriage ways, stable stone and summer tubs
items: A gravel carriage drive now comes in off 18th Street through a gateway in the Pullman wall, as J. W. Taylor's photograph shows it, and up the court to the stable's big arch.
A second drive comes in through the wall's gap east of the house and runs under the porte-cochère to a turning apron, so a carriage can reach the side door.
No shrub stands in any gateway or drive now: the 18th Street border starts east of the house, where the c.1900 photograph shows it.

The stable and the palm house range are one stone now, read from the winter photograph against the house's own walls: a little darker than the stable was built, and much darker than the palm house range's pale stone.
The 1894 plate's summer tub plants stand on and before the palm house's terrace, with a slim clipped evergreen by the wall. Switch the Season to winter and the tubs are gone.
